statement.p: (a) Determine whether function whose values are given in the table below could be linear or exponential.
Find a possible formula for this function.
(b) Determine whether function whose values are given in the table below could be linear or exponential.
Find a possible formula for this function.

static.solution:
SOLUTION
(a) If a function is linear, then the differences in successive function values will be constant. If a function is exponential, the ratios of successive function values will remain constant. Now h(1) - h(0) = 13.5 - 15 = -1.5, and h(2) - h(1) = 12.15 - 13.5 = -1.35 (and similarly for the remaining intervals). Thus, h(x) is not linear.
On the other hand, \begin{aligned} \frac{h(1)}{h(0)} \amp = 0.9\\ \frac{h(2)}{h(1)} \amp = 0.9 \end{aligned} (and similarly for the remaining intervals). Thus h(x) is exponential.
We know that h(x) is exponential, so h(x) = a\,b^x for some constants a and b. We know that h(0)=15, so \begin{aligned} 15 \amp = h(0)\\ 15 \amp = ab^0\\ 15 \amp = a(1). \end{aligned} Thus, a=15. Also \begin{aligned} 13.5 \amp = h(1)\\ 13.5 \amp = 15\,b. \end{aligned} Thus b = 0.9, and we have h(x) = 15\cdot 0.9^x.
(b) As before, if a function is linear, then the differences in successive function values will be constant. If a function is exponential, the ratios of successive function values will remain constant. Now i(1) - i(0) = 18 - 24 = -6, and i(2) - i(1) = 12 - 18 = -6 (and similarly for the remaining intervals). Thus, i(x) is linear.
We know that i(x) is exponential, so i(x) = m\,x + b for some constants m and b. We know that i(0) = 24, so 24 = m\cdot 0 + b = b, and b = 24. Then i(1) = 18, so 18 = m\cdot 1 + 24, so m = 18 - 24 = -6, and we have i(x) = -6\,x + 24.
